arxiv-2105-11886.title: Conformal Anomaly Detection on Spatio-Temporal Observations with Missing Data
arxiv-2105-11886.creator: Chen Xu Yao Xie
arxiv-2105-11886.description: Abstract We develop a distribution-free, unsupervised anomaly detection method called ECAD , which wraps around any regression algorithm and sequentially detects anomalies. Rooted in conformal prediction, ECAD does not require data exchangeability but approximately controls the Type-I error when data are normal. Computationally, it involves no data-splitting and efficiently trains ensemble predictors to increase statistical power.

arxiv-2205-07316.title: MS-TP-22-15 A tower of hidden sectors: a general treatment and physics implications
arxiv-2205-07316.creator: Amin Aboubrahim and Pran Nath
arxiv-2205-07316.description: Abstract An analysis of a tower of hidden sectors coupled to each other, with one of these hidden sectors coupled to the visible sector, is given and the implications of such couplings on physics in the visible sector are investigated.

arxiv-2206-05775.title: Imagination-augmented Navigation Based on 2D Laser Sensor Observations
arxiv-2206-05775.creator: Zhengcheng Shen, Linh Kästner, Magdalena Yordanova, Jens Lambrecht
arxiv-2206-05775.description: Abstract Autonomous navigation of mobile robots is an essential task for various industries. Sensor data is crucial to ensure safe and reliable navigation. However, sensor observations are often limited by different factors. Imagination can assist to enhance the view and aid navigation in dangerous or unknown situations where only limited sensor observation is available.

arxiv-2206-08501.title: Towards Data Assimilation in Level-Set Wildfire Models Using Bayesian Filtering
arxiv-2206-08501.creator: Joel Janek Dabrowski, Carolyn Huston, James Hilton, Stéphane Mangeon, Petra KuhnertData61, CSIROAustralia Firstname.Lastname@data61.csiro.au
arxiv-2206-08501.description: Abstract The level-set method is a prominent approach to modelling the evolution of a fire over time based on a characterised rate of spread. It however does not provide a direct means for assimilating new data and quantifying uncertainty. Fire front predictions can be more accurate and agile if the models are able to assimilate data in real time.

arxiv-2209-13689.title: Optimally Biased Expertise We are grateful to Jean-Michel Benkert, Alessandro Ispano, Meg Meyer, Allen Vong, seminar participants at Bern, Copenhagen, EPFL, CERGE-EI, NRU HSE, and THEMA Cergy, as well as 12th Conference on Economic Design, Oligo Workshop 2022, SAET 2022, and YEM 2022 conference part
arxiv-2209-13689.creator: Pavel Ilinov, Andrei Matveenko, Maxim Senkov, Egor Starkov
arxiv-2209-13689.description: Abstract This paper shows that the principal can strictly benefit from delegating a decision to an agent whose opinion differs from that of the principal. We consider a “delegated expertise” problem, in which the agent has an advantage in information acquisition relative to the principal, as opposed to having preexisting private information.

arxiv-2211-04134.title: Consistent Query Answering for Primary Keys and Conjunctive Queries with Counting
arxiv-2211-04134.creator: Aziz Amezian El Khalfioui, Jef Wijsen
arxiv-2211-04134.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aziz Amezian El Khalfioui, Jef Wijsen. The problem of consistent query answering for primary keys and self-join-free conjunctive queries has been intensively studied in recent years and is by now well understood. In this paper, we study an extension of this problem with counting. The queries we consider count how many times each value occurs in a designated (possibly composite) column of an answer to a full conjunctive query.

arxiv-2307-00251.title: Local Eviction Moratoria and the Spread of COVID-19 Thanks: Julia Hatamyar, Centre for Health Economics, University of York. Christopher F. Parmeter, Department of Economics, University of Miami, Coral Gables, FL 33146; Corresponding Author e-mail: julia.hatamyar@york.ac.uk All R and Stata code used
arxiv-2307-00251.creator: Julia Hatamyar, Christopher F. Parmeter
arxiv-2307-00251.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Julia Hatamyar, Christopher F. Parmeter. At various stages during the initial onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, various US states and local municipalities enacted eviction moratoria. One of the main aims of these moratoria was to slow the spread of COVID-19 infections. We deploy a semiparametric difference-in-differences approach with an event study specification to test whether the lifting of these local moratoria led to an increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths.

arxiv-2308-05413.title: Scattering of relativistic electrons and analogies with optical phenomena: A study of longitudinal and transverse shifts at step potentials
arxiv-2308-05413.creator: Yue Ban, Xi Chen
arxiv-2308-05413.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yue Ban, Xi Chen. We investigate the behavior of relativistic electrons encountering a potential step through analogies with optical phenomena. By accounting for the conservation of Dirac current, we elucidate that the Goos-Hänchen shift can be understood as a combination of two components: one arising from the current entering the transmission region and the other originating from the interference between the incident and reflected beams. This result has been proven to be consistent with findings obtained utilizing the stationary phase method.

arxiv-2403-01651.title: Dagger n n -categories
arxiv-2403-01651.creator: Giovanni Ferrer, Brett Hungar, Theo Johnson-Freyd, Cameron Krulewski, Lukas Müller, Nivedita, David Penneys, David Reutter, Claudia Scheimbauer, Luuk Stehouwer, Chetan Vuppulury
arxiv-2403-01651.description: Abstract . Category theory provides a unified language for organizing composable operations in many disciplines. In disciplines where unitarity is fundamental—such as functional analysis, quantum field theory, and quantum logic—this language must also capture adjoints, leading to the notion of dagger categories.

arxiv-2405-01789.title: Quantifying the Causal Effect of Financial Literacy Courses on Financial Health
arxiv-2405-01789.creator: Arnav Gangal, Charles Shaviro, Daniel Frees
arxiv-2405-01789.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate the causal effect of financial literacy education on a composite financial health score constructed from 17 self-reported financial health and distress metrics ranging from spending habits to confidence in ability to repay debt to day-to-day financial skill.

arxiv-2406-13671.title: Topological Equivalence Theorem and Double-Copy for Chern-Simons Scattering Amplitudes
arxiv-2406-13671.creator: Yan-Feng Hang, Hong-Jian He, Cong Shen 1,
arxiv-2406-13671.description: Abstract We study the mechanism of topological mass-generation for 3d Chern-Simons gauge theories and propose a brand-new Topological Equivalence Theorem to connect scattering amplitudes of the physical gauge boson states to that of the transverse states under high energy expansion.

arxiv-2410-15597.title: A Comprehensive Comparative Study of Individual ML Models and Ensemble Strategies for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
arxiv-2410-15597.creator: Ismail Bibers, Osvaldo Arreche, Mustafa Abdallah
arxiv-2410-15597.description: Abstract The escalating frequency of intrusions in networked systems has spurred the exploration of new research avenues in devising artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for intrusion detection systems (IDS). Various AI techniques have been used to automate network intrusion detection tasks, yet each model possesses distinct strengths and weaknesses.

pmc-10770666.title: Relationship between Delayed Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Behavioral Economic Factors and Personality Characteristics
pmc-10770666.creator: Yoshiaki Shinden, Kayo Kamimura, Naoki Hayashi, Yuki Nomoto, Ayako Nagata, Yuka Eguchi, Hanako Yano, Hazuki Saho, Akihiro Nakajo, Koji Minami, Tadahioro Hirashima, Ken Sasaki, Heiji Yoshinaka, Tetsuhiro Owaki, Akihide Tanimoto, Masayuki Nakamura, Takao Ohtsuka
pmc-10770666.description: Background:Delays in breast cancer diagnosis can allow the disease to progress to an incurable stage. However, factors that cause patients to delay seeking treatment are unclear. In this study, we aimed to identify behavioral economic factors and personality characteristics of patients with breast cancer who had a delayed diagnosis. Methods:We analyzed questionnaires completed by 41 patients with breast cancer.

pmc-11313750.title: Prevalence and Predictors of Food Insecurity among Adults with Type 1 Diabetes: Observational Findings from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System
pmc-11313750.creator: Julie Ann Wagner, Angela Bermúdez-Millán, Richard S Feinn, Maria Kapsokefalou
pmc-11313750.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The majority of data on food insecurity in diabetes comes from samples of type 2 diabetes or youth with type 1 diabetes. This study screened for food insecurity among adults with type 1 diabetes in the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance Survey, which was the first year that respondents who endorsed diabetes were asked to indicate whether they had type 1 or type 2.

pmc-11385829.title: IDH2 regulates macrophage polarization and tumorigenesis by modulating mitochondrial metabolism in macrophages
pmc-11385829.creator: Sung Woo Lee, Soyoon Kim, Bokyung Kim, Jung Bae Seong, Young-Ho Park, Hong Jun Lee, Dong Kyu Choi, Eunbyul Yeom, Dong-Seok Lee
pmc-11385829.description: BackgroundTargeting the tumor microenvironment represents an emerging therapeutic strategy for cancer. Macrophages are an essential part of the tumor microenvironment. Macrophage polarization is modulated by mitochondrial metabolism, including oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and reactive oxygen species content. Isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2), an enzyme involved in the TCA cycle, reportedly promotes cancer progression.

pmc-11416688.title: Dissolution of EAF slag minerals in aqueous media: Effects of sonication on brownmillerite and gehlenite
pmc-11416688.creator: Recep Kurtulus, Mahtab Akbarzadeh Khoei, Elijah Damilola Adesanya, Juho Yliniemi
pmc-11416688.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The accumulation of electric arc furnace slag (EAFS) in landfills has been causing severe environmental problems. This study examines the dissolution properties of EAFS minerals, including brownmillerite and gehlenite, essential for their possible use in resource recovery. An investigation was conducted to compare the effects of sonication and stirring on mineral dissolution while also assessing the usage of citrate as a complexing agent for gehlenite.

pmc-12486387.title: A Multi Clone Kinetic Model for characterizing Chinese hamster ovary cell line variability
pmc-12486387.creator: Devi Sietaram, Pavlos Kotidis, Gary Finka, Alexei A Lapkin
pmc-12486387.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper presents the Multi Clone Kinetic Model (MCKM), a novel generalized kinetic mechanistic model for fed-batch cultivations of diverse Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell lines, producing different recombinant monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Unlike traditional kinetic models requiring multiple cultures for one parameter regression, MCKM derives a complete set of 13 kinetic parameters from a single fed-batch cell line culture of 49 data points.

pmc-12554974.title: Effects of different packaging on dried sword prawn (Parapenaeopsis hardwickii) quality, flavor, microbial communities, and lipid profiles during chilled storage: An integrated analysis
pmc-12554974.creator: Wenxiong Zheng, Feili Zhan, Shanshan Shui, Ronglin Yang, Yi Hu, Zhengxuan Qin, Soottawat Benjakul, Bin Zhang
pmc-12554974.description: This study examined the impact of common packaging (CP), vacuum packaging (VP), and nitrogen packaging (NP) on muscle quality, volatile compounds, microbial communities, and lipid profiles in dried Parapenaeopsis hardwickii during 120 d of storage at 4 °C, using physicochemical analysis, HS-SPME-GC–MS, high-throughput sequencing, and lipidomics.

pmc-12625377.title: Exploring the lived experiences of children in relation to trauma and violence exposure in the Vhembe district
pmc-12625377.creator: Petunia Tsheole, Lufuno Makhado, Angelina Maphula, Nombulelo Veronica Sepeng
pmc-12625377.description: BackgroundViolence and trauma exposure among children remain critical public health issues, particularly in under-resourced regions such as the Vhembe district, South Africa. Although much is known about the prevalence of child abuse, limited research explores children’s lived experiences and coping mechanisms from their own perspectives.

pmc-12682903.title: Enhanced bioproduction of phenolic compounds from Populus nigra L. using temporary immersion bioreactors and metabolomics
pmc-12682903.creator: Malorie Laffon, Florent Magot, Caroline Birer Williams, Franck Michoux, Clément Lemoine, Arnaud Lanoue, Nathalie Giglioli-Guivarc’h
pmc-12682903.description: Black poplar is a woody species rich in bioactive phenolic compounds with promising pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications. In wild populations, genetic diversity and environmental variability affect phenolic content and bioactivities. Plant tissue culture, conducted under controlled conditions, offers a suitable alternative for industrial bioproduction.

pmc-13181065.title: Non-O157 shiga toxin–producing Escherichia coli (STEC) in Africa: a one health systematic review and meta-analysis of prevalence, antimicrobial resistance, and clinical outcomes
pmc-13181065.creator: Paul Akinniyi Akinduti, Alex Odoom, Samuel Darkwah, Emmanuel Nnabuike Ugbo, Yaw Aniweh, Eric S. Donkor
pmc-13181065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Non-O157 Shiga Toxin–Producing Escherichia coli (non-O157 STEC) pathogens cause considerable debilities and were reviewed for its prevalence, antimicrobial Resistance, and clinical outcomes in Africa from a One Health perspective. Following the PRISMA guidelines, studies reporting non-O157 STEC in human, animal, environmental and food samples from African countries were retrieved from African Journals Online, Scopus, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and PubMed. Retrieved data were analyzed using random-effects model by the DerSimonian–Laird method and assessment of risk-of-bias for individual studies, with Egger’s test.
